summary: Île Sainte-Marie light, Lower North Shore: a 1913 concrete tower with a fourth-order lens, Osborne family keepers, a 1981 steel tower, now in a seabird sanctuary.

lens.note: Fourth-order dioptric lens of the 1913-14 installation (Department table, St. Marys Isle row for FY ending March 1914; checked on the page image). LighthouseFriends: a revolving fourth-order lens on the concrete tower.

light.note: Current light on a steel skeleton tower; the Coast Guard lists it as seasonal (entry 1562). The 1913 light showed two flashes every fifteen seconds (LighthouseFriends).

structures.note: Hexagonal reinforced concrete tower, no longer an aid to navigation (register). Height disputed: 29 ft (8.8 m) per LighthouseFriends; 15 ft (4.6 m) in the 1913 Department table (St. Mary island row, checked on the page image); barely 5 m (16.5 ft) per the register.
Square skeleton tower carrying the present light.
Fog-alarm building with a diaphone, added 1920-21 (LighthouseFriends).

Wooden dwelling in the 1913 Department table (St. Mary island row). LighthouseFriends describes a two-storey keepers' dwelling with a couple of outbuildings; the register counts two residences, several buildings in ruins.

access.note: Coast Guard lighthouse; grounds and tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Offshore, about 20 km from Harrington Harbour, in a migratory bird sanctuary; visitors are asked to read the restrictions first.

notes_for_editor: 1) Checked on the page images. The 1913 new-aids table (scan p. 53) has four Quebec rows (Ferolle point, Flat island, Natashkwan, St. Mary island). The St. Mary island row is the fourth: a 15-foot reinforced concrete tower and wooden dwelling, F. E. Cote, $5,315.63. The 4-foot tower with double dwelling, fog-alarm building, oil store, boat house and road and the illuminating-apparatus sentence belong to Ferolle point, so the earlier draft misattributed them; they are removed. 2) The 1914 table (scan p. 51) has St. Marys Isle as the second row, with the completion of the concrete tower and dwelling and a 4th order dioptric lens, F. E. Cote. 3) 1921 (scan p. 33) and 1922 (scan p. 31): St. Mary island sits under the Prince Edward Island heading, not Quebec. The 1923 and 1924 entries (printed pp. 27 and 29) were read from the OCR order under the same Prince Edward Island heading, not from the page image. 4) Sessional Paper numbers: the 1913, 1914 and 1921 reports are No. 21; the reports for FY 1922, 1923 and 1924 are No. 28 (OCR running heads in the 1923, 1924 and 1925 volumes). 5) Tower height: 8.8 m (LighthouseFriends), 4.6 m (1913 table), barely 5 m (register). The record's 16.4 m is the 1981 steel tower, not the 1913 tower. 6) The 1922 Deputy Minister's report calls the station 'St. Mary island (Labrador)' among four new apparatus; the register and the Quebec headings place it in Quebec. 7) Keepers: LighthouseFriends is the only keeper list read; Quebec keeper tables for 1913-1925 were not legible in the corpus. Donald G. Osborne's connection with this station ended in 1956; his later Souris service is given only as LighthouseFriends prints it. 8) No wreck, storm or rescue tied to the station in the sources read; the storms chapter is omitted. No source gives a year for the station's automation; the story says only that the register calls it automated now. 9) First lighting date not found in the sources read; the record's first_lit is null. 10) Record: visit.grounds_open true vs LighthouseFriends 'Grounds/tower closed'. 11) LighthouseFriends is copyrighted; the story paraphrases it and quotes no sentence from it. The 1984 interview is cited through it. 12) Trinity House and Quebec newspapers were not read. No photos sourced.
